newsitem.title: INDIA: India seen little affected by Thai currency float.
newsitem.headline: India seen little affected by Thai currency float.

text.p: The fall in the Thai baht after the country's decision to float its currency will have little or no impact on India, dealers and analysts said on Thursday.
The baht fell around 15-20 percent on Wednesday after Thailand decided to float its currency after 13 years of pegging it to a basket of currencies.
Other south east Asian currencies came under speculative pressure following the fall in the baht but dealers said the Indian currency was safe from such attacks.
"Basically we have to remember that (foreign investor) fund allocations to India and Thailand come from two different baskets," said Ramnath Iyer, strategist at Peregrine Capital India Ltd.
"India comes under the emerging markets basket while Thailand comes under the Asian markets basket," Iyer said.
Indian forex dealers said they did not anticipate any immediate inflow or outflow of foreign funds.

"I think any impact will be mainly felt by ASEAN countries," said the chief dealer at a European bank. "Where India is concerned, it is the events in our immediate neighbours such as Pakistan and Bangladesh which will affect us."
Another dealer said the floating of the baht had removed uncertainty and there could be a marginal flow of funds out of India to Thailand.
"Earlier there was some uncertainty what would happen in Thailand," the dealer said. "Some funds may have come from there to India and these will now flow back now that the baht has depreciated."
The fall in the baht will make Thai stocks more attractive and could attract funds which had flown out, back into the country, he said.
